_note: MJ LOOK PRESETS — thirty film/format/emulation looks, one per entry. The registry is canonical: the pack and the doc are GENERATED from it, never hand-copied.
_note_what_this_is: A LOOK is the era, the stock and the texture of the IMAGE — not the scene and not the subject. The existing lib/mj-scene-presets.json holds SCENES (a physical event, a light, a frame); this file holds the LOOK that is laid over a scene. A scene preset and a look preset are different objects and they live in different files.
_note_test_method: THE TEST IS A COMPARISON, NOT A SHOWCASE. Every entry renders the SAME anchor subject, so the only variable across the thirty is the look. That is what makes the sheet a test: any difference between two cells is the look's doing. The anchor subject was chosen to be neutral — a figure, a wall, a light source — so a look cannot be credited for the subject it happens to be handed.
title: MJ Look Presets
subtitle: 30 film, video-tape and emulation looks · one anchor subject · a comparison sheet
anchor: A man in a dark overcoat stands alone in a bare room beside a single window, a wooden chair in the middle of the floor, dust in the air
_note_anchor: THE ANCHOR SUBJECT. One figure, one chair, one window, bare walls — deliberately plain. Every look renders this, so the sheet compares the looks and not the subjects. It is also neutral enough that no look can be credited for a subject it happened to be handed: there is no neon sign to justify a neon preset, no wet street for the rain look, no period costume for a 1940s look.
_note_anchor_clauses: The anchor is stored as a LIST of clauses, not one sentence, because the pack needs to REORDER them per prompt. The subject is shared by all thirty, so every prompt would open with the same words — and a shared prefix collapses the acceptance matcher's excerpt, which is how N prompts get attributed to a few task ids (measured 2026-09-24 → 2026-11-05). The composer rotates the opening clause, so each prompt still renders the SAME scene but starts differently.
anchorClauses: A man in a dark overcoat stands alone in a bare room
a wooden chair in the middle of the floor
_note_openings: EACH PRESET GETS ITS OWN OPENING PHRASE. The subject is shared by all thirty, so a fixed clause order would open every prompt with the same words — and a shared prefix collapses the acceptance matcher's excerpt, which is how N prompts get attributed to a few task ids (measured 2026-09-24 → 2026-11-05). Rotating four clauses was tried first and produced only FOUR distinct openings, which is not enough for thirty. So each preset carries a short, distinct opening that names the same scene from a different angle, and the rest of the anchor follows it.

_note_suffix: The house negation — signage and lettering stay out, so a look like CCTV or Betacam does not spend its budget on text.
_note_flags: The house values, stated explicitly so the composed prompt carries exactly one --ar and one --s. The house value is --s 21 (the artist: "the literal-photo reference is the goal, stylize is the enemy"). Per the registry rules, a LOOK PRESET carries no flags of its own — the pack owns them. `--ar` IS LAST ON PURPOSE: Midjourney honours the LAST occurrence of a duplicated flag (the bug class this repo has hit three times), so the ratio goes at the end.

_note_families: The families are the useful grouping for a user choosing a look: film-analog (14), video-tape (3), digital-video (2), digital-documentary (2), surveillance (2). Nothing depends on the family — it is documentation.
_note_ratios: Each look carries its NATIVE ratio — the frame shape is part of what the medium IS. A cut is ONE ratio (the renderer takes one --size for a whole cut), so a plan spanning several ratios is REFUSED rather than silently scaled. The pack's --ar overrides the ratio for a look plate; the cut plan's --ar-filter selects which looks may share a cut.
_note_rendered: THE RENDERED SET. Every look was rendered from the same anchor subject, so any difference between two frames is the LOOK's doing. Each entry carries the cell the measurement screen picked (the one closest to the median luma, never a blown one over 90) and that cell's luma. TWO LOOKS HAVE EVERY CELL BLOWN (19 Expired Polaroid, 24 Desert Mirage) — for those the sheet shows the LEAST-blown cell and says so, because an overexposed frame IS the look in both cases.
